question: Who was the revenue minister of Akbar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Todar Mal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raja Todar Mal was the revenue/finance minister (Diwan-i-Ashraf / Mal Guzari) of Emperor Akbar and one of his Navratnas (nine gems).

• He introduced the Dahsala/Zabti (bandobast) revenue system (राजस्व प्रणाली), standardising land measurement and fixing revenue as an average of ten years' produce.

• He also made Persian the official language of revenue records.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The land was classified into Polaj, Parauti, Chachar and Banjar based on cultivation continuity.

• Todar Mal earlier served under Sher Shah Suri, whose revenue reforms he refined for Akbar.

• Akbar's Navratnas also included Abul Fazl, Faizi, Tansen, Birbal, Man Singh, Bhagwan Das, Mullah Do-Piyaza and Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana.

NOTE

• Raja Bharmal (Option 1): Kachhwaha ruler of Amber who was the first Rajput king to ally with Akbar through a matrimonial alliance.

• Birbal (Option 2): One of Akbar's Navratnas, famous as a witty courtier and administrator; he died in the Yusufzai campaign.

• Raja Man Singh (Option 3): A trusted Kachhwaha general (Navratna) of Akbar who led campaigns in Bengal and against Maharana Pratap at Haldighati.

question:
As of 31st July 2025, which of the following is the official language of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation?
I. Russian
II. Hindi
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) has only two official/working languages — Russian and Chinese (रूसी और चीनी).

• Among the given statements, only Russian is an official language; Hindi is not an SCO official language.

• Hence statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect, making Only I the answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The SCO was founded in 2001 in Shanghai; its permanent Secretariat is in Beijing, China.

• India became a full member in 2018 along with Pakistan; Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024.

• SCO's official languages being only Russian and Chinese is a frequently repeated fact in exams.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong because Hindi is not an SCO official language.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong because only Russian (not Hindi) qualifies.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Wrong because Russian is indeed an SCO official language.

question: The East Asia Summit process was initiated in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The East Asia Summit (EAS) process was initiated in 2005 (पूर्वी एशिया शिखर सम्मेलन), with the first summit held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on 14 December 2005.

• It is a leaders-led forum for strategic dialogue on political, security and economic issues in the Indo-Pacific.

• India is a founding member of the EAS.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The EAS is ASEAN-centred, with ASEAN in the driving seat.

• Members: 10 ASEAN nations plus Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia and the USA (18 in total).

• Priority cooperation areas include environment/energy, education, finance, health, disaster management and connectivity.

NOTE

• 1999 (Option 1): Year the ASEAN Plus Three (APT) cooperation process began, not the EAS.

• 2002 (Option 2): Not the initiation year of the EAS.

• 2003 (Option 3): Not associated with the EAS launch.

question: Who wrote 'The Jungle Book' in 1894?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudyard Kipling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The Jungle Book' (द जंगल बुक) was written by British author Rudyard Kipling and published in 1894.

• It is a collection of stories, most famously featuring the man-cub Mowgli raised by wolves, along with Baloo, Bagheera and Shere Khan.

• Kipling was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1907, becoming its first English-language recipient.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kipling was born in Bombay (Mumbai), India, in 1865.

• Other notable works: 'The Second Jungle Book' (1895), 'Kim', 'Just So Stories' and the poem 'If—'.

• Much of the Jungle Book is set in the forests of central India.

NOTE

• William Shakespeare (Option 2): English playwright/poet of the 16th–17th century, author of Hamlet, Macbeth and Romeo and Juliet.

• Stephen Alter (Option 3): Indian-American author born in Mussoorie, known for nature and Himalayan writing.

• Edgar Allan Poe (Option 4): American writer famed for mystery and macabre tales like 'The Raven' and 'The Tell-Tale Heart'.

question: _____ assumed the office of Director General of Defence Estates on May 31, 2025.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shailendra Nath Gupta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shailendra Nath Gupta, a senior Indian Defence Estates Service (IDES) officer, assumed charge as Director General of Defence Estates (रक्षा संपदा महानिदेशक) on 31 May 2025.

• The Directorate General of Defence Estates functions under the Ministry of Defence and manages defence lands and cantonments.

• The appointment is a repeatedly asked 2025 current-affairs fact.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The DGDE oversees management of defence land records, cantonment administration and land digitisation initiatives.

• The office headquarters is located in New Delhi.

• IDES is a Group 'A' civil service of the Ministry of Defence.

NOTE

• Alok Joshi (Option 1): Former R&AW chief who was appointed as Chairman of the reconstituted National Security Advisory Board (NSAB) in 2025.

• Mayank Sharma (Option 3): Not the DG of Defence Estates.

• Justice Arun Palli (Option 4): A judge (Chief Justice of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court), unrelated to Defence Estates.

question: How many authors are to be selected under the PM-YUVA 3.0?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under PM-YUVA 3.0 (प्रधानमंत्री युवा लेखक मेंटरशिप योजना), a total of 50 young authors are to be selected and mentored.

• YUVA stands for Young, Upcoming and Versatile Authors, a mentorship scheme to train budding writers under the age of 30.

• It is an initiative of the Ministry of Education implemented through the National Book Trust (NBT).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme aims to promote reading, writing and book culture and to project India and Indian writings globally.

• Selected authors receive a monthly scholarship during the mentorship period.

• It supports the vision of making India a hub for content creation.

NOTE

• 30 (Option 1): Not the number of authors selected under PM-YUVA 3.0.

• 60 (Option 3): Incorrect figure for the scheme.

• 65 (Option 4): Incorrect figure for the scheme.

question: How many sections does the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 contain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 358.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 (भारतीय न्याय संहिता) contains 358 sections.

• It replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860 and came into force on 1 July 2024.

• The BNS is the new substantive criminal law of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The IPC had 511 sections; the BNS consolidates these into 358 sections.

• Two companion laws: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) replaced the CrPC, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) replaced the Indian Evidence Act.

• The BNS introduced new offences such as those relating to organised crime, terrorism and mob lynching.

NOTE

• 558 (Option 2): Not the number of sections in the BNS.

• 258 (Option 3): Incorrect count of BNS sections.

• 458 (Option 4): Incorrect count of BNS sections.

question: As the Atal Pension Yojana completed 10 years in May 2025, which age group is eligible to enroll in the scheme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18-40 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) (अटल पेंशन योजना), any Indian citizen aged 18 to 40 years with a bank/post office account can enrol.

• The scheme completed 10 years in May 2025 (launched on 9 May 2015).

• It provides a guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 after the age of 60.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• APY is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

• The pension amount depends on the contribution and the age of joining; contributions continue up to age 60.

• It primarily targets workers in the unorganised sector.

NOTE

• 21-50 years (Option 2): Incorrect eligibility band; the upper limit for joining is 40, not 50.

• 18-60 years (Option 3): 60 is the age at which pension begins, not the joining age limit.

• 25-65 years (Option 4): Not the eligibility range prescribed for APY enrolment.

question: What was the rank of Harvard University in Global University Employability Ranking 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harvard University was ranked 4th in the Global University Employability Ranking 2025 (वैश्विक विश्वविद्यालय रोजगार क्षमता रैंकिंग).

• The ranking is published by Times Higher Education in partnership with the HR consultancy Emerging, based on a survey of recruiters/employers.

• MIT topped the list at 1st place in 2025.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 2025 top order was MIT (1), Caltech (2), Stanford (3), Harvard (4).

• The ranking measures how well universities prepare graduates for employment as judged by global employers.

• Indian institutions like IITs and IISc also feature among globally ranked universities in various such surveys.

NOTE

• 1st (Option 1): Held by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), not Harvard.

• 2nd (Option 2): Held by the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

• 3rd (Option 3): Held by Stanford University.

question: In which of the following Summer Olympics did Neeraj Chopra win the gold medal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal in javelin throw (भाला फेंक) at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics (held in 2021).

• His winning throw was 87.58 metres.

• He became the first Indian to win an Olympic gold in athletics and only the second individual Olympic gold medallist for India (after Abhinav Bindra).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• At the Paris 2024 Olympics, Neeraj Chopra won the silver medal in javelin throw.

• He also won gold at the 2022 Diamond League final and the 2023 World Athletics Championships.

• He hails from Khandra village, Panipat district, Haryana.

NOTE

• 2016 (Option 1): Rio Olympics; Neeraj Chopra did not compete for a medal there (he won the World U-20 title that year).

• 2024 (Option 3): Paris Olympics, where he won silver, not gold.

• 2008 (Option 4): Beijing Olympics, where Abhinav Bindra won India's shooting gold; unrelated to Neeraj Chopra.

question: Strokes, Starts and Turns are some of the Techniques of which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swimming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Strokes, Starts and Turns are fundamental techniques of Swimming (तैराकी).

• Strokes include freestyle (front crawl), backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.

• Starts (dive/push-off) and Turns (like the tumble turn) are key to racing performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Competitive swimming is governed globally by World Aquatics (formerly FINA).

• A standard Olympic swimming pool is 50 metres long.

• Michael Phelps of the USA is the most decorated Olympian, largely through swimming.

NOTE

• Baseball (Option 2): Uses terms like pitching, batting, innings and home runs.

• Golf (Option 3): Uses terms like putt, birdie, bogey, tee and caddie.

• Badminton (Option 4): Uses terms like smash, drop, service, deuce and shuttlecock.

question: To protect one-horned rhinos from poachers which state has launched the Operation Falcon in August 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Assam (असम) launched Operation Falcon in August 2025 to protect the one-horned rhinoceros from poachers and to crack down on rhino-horn trafficking networks.

• The one-horned rhino (Rhinoceros unicornis) is the state animal of Assam and is chiefly found in Kaziranga National Park.

• The operation targeted illegal wildlife trade syndicates.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kaziranga National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and hosts the largest population of one-horned rhinos.

• Other rhino habitats in Assam include Orang, Pobitora and Manas National Parks.

• The one-horned rhino is listed as 'Vulnerable' on the IUCN Red List.

NOTE

• Uttarakhand (Option 2): Known for Jim Corbett and Rajaji National Parks (tigers/elephants), not one-horned rhino conservation.

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): The 'Tiger State', home to Kanha and Bandhavgarh, not rhinos.

• Karnataka (Option 4): Known for Bandipur and Nagarhole reserves; not a one-horned rhino habitat.

question: The Umred-Pauni-Karhandla Sanctuary, is in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Umred-Pauni-Karhandla Wildlife Sanctuary (उमरेड-पौनी-करहांडला अभयारण्य) is located in Maharashtra, spread across the Nagpur and Bhandara districts.

• It is a well-known tiger habitat connected to the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve landscape.

• It is famous for wildlife tourism and tiger sightings.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The sanctuary supports tigers, leopards, wild dogs, sloth bears and various deer species.

• It acts as a wildlife corridor in the central Indian tiger landscape.

• Maharashtra's other major reserves include Tadoba-Andhari, Pench (Maharashtra) and Melghat.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 2): Home to Gir (Asiatic lions) and the Wild Ass Sanctuary in the Rann of Kutch.

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Home to Corbett and Rajaji National Parks.

• Punjab (Option 4): Has wetland sanctuaries like Harike, not the Umred-Pauni-Karhandla sanctuary.

question: The National Marathon in February 2025, was held in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Marathon in February 2025 was held in New Delhi (नई दिल्ली), the national capital.

• Marathons in the capital are commonly organised along landmark routes and promote fitness and mass participation.

• The event aligned with the government's Fit India movement objectives.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A full marathon covers a distance of 42.195 km.

• New Delhi regularly hosts major running events such as the Delhi Half Marathon.

• Such events support the national push for sports and physical fitness.

NOTE

• Chennai (Option 2): Capital of Tamil Nadu; not the venue for this National Marathon.

• Chandigarh (Option 3): Union Territory and joint capital of Punjab and Haryana; not the host.

• Kolkata (Option 4): Capital of West Bengal; not the venue for the February 2025 National Marathon.

question: 'Dewar Geet', sung as entertainment songs, are associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Dewar Geet' (देवार गीत) are folk entertainment songs associated with the state of Chhattisgarh.

• They are sung by the Dewar community, a traditional wandering/minstrel community of the region.

• The songs form part of Chhattisgarh's rich folk-music heritage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other famous Chhattisgarhi folk songs include Sua Geet, Karma, Pandwani and Bhojali.

• Pandwani is a famous ballad narrating the Mahabharata; Teejan Bai is its renowned exponent.

• Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November 2000, carved out of Madhya Pradesh.

NOTE

• Goa (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Mando, Dulpod and Fugdi.

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Known for Lavani, Powada and Koli folk songs.

• Haryana (Option 3): Known for Ragini and Saang folk traditions.

question: The diameter of the bamboo flutes is usually about _____ cm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.9.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The diameter of bamboo flutes (बांस की बांसुरी) is usually about 1.9 cm.

• The flute (bansuri) is a side-blown aerophone wind instrument made from a single hollow shaft of bamboo.

• Its diameter and length determine the pitch and tonal quality of the instrument.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The bansuri is closely associated with Lord Krishna in Indian tradition.

• Renowned exponents include Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia and Pannalal Ghosh.

• The flute typically has six or seven finger holes plus a blowing hole.

NOTE

• 4.1 (Option 2): Larger than the typical bamboo flute diameter; incorrect.

• 4.8 (Option 3): Too large a diameter for a standard bamboo flute.

• 3.8 (Option 4): Overstates the usual bamboo flute diameter.

question: What were the cities of the Indus Valley generally enclosed with?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fortified walls with gateways.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation (सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता) were generally enclosed with fortified walls with gateways, mostly made of baked and mud bricks.

• Many cities had a raised, walled Citadel on the west and a Lower Town to the east.

• The fortifications served administrative, defensive and flood-control purposes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan and Rakhigarhi.

• The civilisation is noted for its grid-pattern town planning and advanced drainage systems.

• The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro is a famous example of its public architecture.

NOTE

• Wooden fences (Option 1): Not used; Indus cities relied on brick fortifications, not timber enclosures.

• Stone barricades (Option 3): Indus cities mostly used baked/mud bricks rather than stone (except Dholavira's stone use).

• Moats and drawbridges (Option 4): A medieval European castle feature, not characteristic of Indus cities.

question: Which of the following states practices the folk dance form 'Hai-Hak'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Hai-Hak' (हाई-हक) is a folk dance associated with the state of Tripura.

• It is performed by the Halam community of Tripura, usually connected with harvest celebrations.

• Tripura has a vibrant tribal dance tradition tied to agriculture and festivals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other well-known Tripuri folk dances include Hojagiri, Garia, Lebang Boomani and Bizu.

• The Hojagiri dance is performed by women balancing pitchers and lamps on their heads.

• Tripura became a full-fledged state on 21 January 1972.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Garba, Dandiya Raas and Bhavai.

• Bihar (Option 3): Known for Jat-Jatin, Bidesia and Jhijhian folk dances.

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Theyyam and Thiruvathira.

question: The International Space Station circles Earth roughly _____ times a day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The International Space Station (ISS) (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अंतरिक्ष स्टेशन) circles the Earth roughly 16 times a day.

• It orbits at an average altitude of about 400 km and travels at around 28,000 km/h.

• It completes one orbit in approximately 90–93 minutes, giving about 16 orbits every 24 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The ISS is a joint project of NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA, JAXA (Japan) and CSA (Canada).

• Astronauts aboard the ISS experience about 16 sunrises and sunsets each day.

• The ISS has been continuously occupied by humans since November 2000.

NOTE

• 36 (Option 1): Too high; the ISS does not complete 36 orbits a day.

• 8 (Option 2): Too few; this would imply an orbital period of about 3 hours.

• 24 (Option 4): Overstates the number of orbits; the ISS orbits about 16 times, not 24.

question: Why does a matchstick catch fire when struck against a rough surface?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because friction produces heat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A matchstick catches fire because friction produces heat (घर्षण से ऊष्मा उत्पन्न होती है) when it is struck against a rough surface.

• The heat generated raises the temperature of the chemicals on the match head to their ignition point.

• The rough striking surface contains red phosphorus, which reacts to start combustion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The match head typically contains an oxidising agent (like potassium chlorate) and sulphur/antimony compounds.

• Friction converts mechanical energy into heat energy, an example of energy transformation.

• In safety matches, the phosphorus is on the striking strip, not the match head.

NOTE

• Because it contains petrol (Option 1): False; matches do not contain petrol.

• Because the stick is hollow (Option 3): Irrelevant and untrue; ignition is due to heat of friction, not shape.

• Because it absorbs moisture (Option 4): Opposite of the truth; moisture actually prevents a match from lighting.

question: In February 2025, which US pharma firm announced a $200 million investment in its technology center in Hyderabad, focusing on AI and data science?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amgen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2025, the US biotechnology/pharma firm Amgen (एम्जेन) announced a $200 million investment in its technology centre in Hyderabad, focusing on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data science.

• The move strengthens Hyderabad's position as a global hub for pharma R&D and technology.

• Amgen is one of the world's leading independent biotechnology companies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hyderabad is often called the 'Genome Valley' and a major pharmaceutical/life-sciences hub of India.

• Amgen is headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California, USA.

• Such investments boost India's digital and biotech innovation ecosystem.

NOTE

• Pfizer (Option 1): US pharma giant known for its COVID-19 vaccine; not the firm in this announcement.

• Merck (Option 3): US pharmaceutical company (MSD outside North America); not linked to this investment.

• Johnson & Johnson (Option 4): US healthcare/consumer-health multinational; not the company in question.

question: Which crop did the British force the peasants of Assam to produce?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tea.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The British forced the peasants of Assam to produce Tea (चाय) by establishing large tea plantations in the 19th century.

• Commercial tea cultivation in Assam began after the discovery of wild tea plants there in the 1820s–1830s.

• The Assam Company (1839) became one of the first joint-stock tea companies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Assam is today the largest tea-producing state in India.

• Labourers were brought in large numbers, often under exploitative indenture-like conditions, to work the plantations.

• Assam and Darjeeling teas are globally renowned varieties.

NOTE

• Cotton (Option 1): The British encouraged cotton mainly in the Deccan/western India, not Assam.

• Wheat (Option 3): A staple food crop, not a colonial plantation crop imposed in Assam.

• Rice (Option 4): A traditional subsistence crop, not the plantation crop forced by the British in Assam.

question: The Indira Gandhi Canal originates at Harike barrage in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indira Gandhi Canal (इंदिरा गांधी नहर) originates at the Harike Barrage in Punjab, located below the confluence of the Satluj and Beas rivers.

• It is one of the longest canals in India, carrying water into the arid Thar Desert region of Rajasthan.

• It was formerly known as the Rajasthan Canal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The canal has greatly transformed agriculture in the desert districts of western Rajasthan (e.g., Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer).

• It consists of a feeder canal and a main canal.

• The project is a landmark example of desert irrigation in India.

NOTE

• Rajasthan (Option 2): The canal irrigates Rajasthan, but it originates (starts) in Punjab, not Rajasthan.

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Source region of the Ganga/Yamuna, unrelated to the Harike barrage.

• Haryana (Option 4): Has canals like the Western Yamuna Canal, but the Indira Gandhi Canal does not originate here.

question: Which religious community had the second-largest population in India as per Census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muslim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the Muslim community (मुस्लिम समुदाय) had the second-largest population in India after Hindus.

• Muslims constituted about 14.2% of India's total population.

• Hindus were the largest at about 79.8%.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Order of religious communities by population (2011): Hindu > Muslim > Christian > Sikh > Buddhist > Jain.

• Christians were about 2.3% and Sikhs about 1.7% of the population.

• The Census of India has been conducted every ten years since 1872 (first synchronous census in 1881).

NOTE

• Christian (Option 1): The third-largest religious community (about 2.3%) as per Census 2011.

• Sikh (Option 2): The fourth-largest community (about 1.7%).

• Buddhist (Option 4): The fifth-largest community (about 0.7%).

question: The philosophical concept that everything in the universe is one divine essence is called _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Brahman (ब्रह्म / ब्रह्मन्) is the philosophical concept in Indian thought that the entire universe is one supreme, ultimate, unchanging divine essence or reality.

• It is a central idea of the Upanishads and Vedanta philosophy.

• The doctrine 'Aham Brahmasmi' (I am Brahman) reflects the identity of the individual soul (Atman) with Brahman.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The mahavakya 'Tat Tvam Asi' (That Thou Art) expresses the unity of Atman and Brahman.

• Adi Shankaracharya propounded Advaita Vedanta (non-dualism) centred on Brahman.

• Brahman (the absolute reality) is different from Brahma (the creator god of the Trimurti).

NOTE

• Samiti (Option 1): A popular assembly/council in Vedic-era polity, not a metaphysical concept of divine essence.

• Yajna (Option 2): A Vedic ritual of sacrifice/offering made into the sacred fire.

• Purandar (Option 3): An epithet of the god Indra (also a fort near Pune); not a philosophical concept of universal essence.
